How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted, and comment
for agenda items 3 and 4 is combined.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three minutes per
person (six minutes if using an interpreter) per item. At the Mayor’s discretion, the time
limit may be shortened to allow all speakers to address the City Council. Please note
that interactions between the City Council, City staff, and the public during meetings
are subject to the City’s Rules of Decorum.

Website: Electronic submission of Public Comment is available via the online public
comment form at Public Comment. Public Comment submitted electronically by 4:00
P.M. on the meeting day will be forwarded to the City Council before the meeting for
their consideration, but will not be read during the meeting. Comments submitted after
4:00 P.M. will be forwarded to Council but may not be received before the meeting.

   City Council Regular Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, February 17, 2026

 •  CALL TO ORDER

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  2. Minutes of the Regular City Council Meeting of February 3, 2026.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as

  Recommended Action: Approval

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented
  to the City Council for review and approval.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 17, 2026  2
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – JANUARY 2026

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2025-2026 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 25-25) and California Government Code Section 53646,
  the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the City Council, City
  Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The Cash and Investment
  Report is presented to receive and file in accordance with the City’s adopted
  2025-2026 Investment Policy.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for January 2026.

  D. EXCHANGE OF PROPOSITION A FUNDS IN THE AMOUNT OF $500,000

  The City of San Gabriel receives about $1 million annually in Proposition A Local
  Return Funds from Los Angeles County to be used for the benefit of public
  transit. The funds may be used to fund the City’s Ride SG and Recreation transit
  programs. For Fiscal Year 2025-26, Proposition C funds are being used to fund
  the program, budgeted at $859,000. As of June 30, 2025, Proposition A has
  $568,000 in fund balance. Los Angeles County Metro allows agencies to
  exchange Proposition A funds for unrestricted General Fund revenue at a
  discounted rate – a practice that San Gabriel has taken advantage of in the past.
  Foothill Transit has offered to exchange $500,000 of the City’s Proposition A
  Funds for $375,000 in unrestricted funds, representing a rate of $.75/$1.00.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 17, 2026  3
   Staff recommends that the City Council approve and authorize the City
  Manager to execute the attached agreement with the Foothill Transit Authority
  authorizing the exchange of $500,000 in Proposition A Funds for $375,000 in
  General Fund revenue.

  E. APPROVAL OF PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT AND STATEMENT
  OF WORK WITH CIVICPLUS FOR CITY WEBSITE REDESIGN, HOSTING, AND
  RELATED DIGITAL SERVICES

  The City of San Gabriel’s official website serves as the primary digital
  communication and service delivery platform for residents, businesses, and
  visitors. The current website has not undergone a comprehensive redesign
  since 2016 and no longer meets modern expectations for usability, accessibility,
  mobile responsiveness, and content management. Following a competitive
  Request for Proposals (RFP No. 23-16) process, CivicPlus was selected as the
  most qualified vendor to provide website redesign, consolidation, hosting, and
  consulting services. Approval of this item will allow the City to modernize its
  website, improve accessibility compliance, enhance cybersecurity, and provide
  a more user-friendly digital experience. Based on the CivicPlus Statement of
  Work, the total initial investment for the first year is estimated at approximately
  $33,219.82. which reflects prorated Year 1 costs. Ongoing annual recurring
  services are estimated at approximately $19,966.00 every July.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  a Professional Services Agreement and associated Statement of Work with
  CivicPlus for the redesign, hosting, and ongoing support of the City of San
  Gabriel website, including related digital services.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. REVIEW VETERANS MEMORIAL CONCEPTUAL DESIGNS AND PROVIDE
  DIRECTION TO STAFF AND LANDSCAPE ARCHITECT DAVID VOLZ DESIGN
  CREATIVE

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 17, 2026  4
   David Volz Design Creative, the Landscape Architect contracted to design the
  San Gabriel Veterans Memorial, met with the San Gabriel Veterans Memorial
  Coalition, staff and the community to gain insight prior to designing the
  memorial. They designed two concepts and presented them to staff and the
  Coalition. Review of the concept designs and providing direction to staff does
  not result in any fiscal impact.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council review Concept Designs 1 and 2 and
  provide direction for any recommended revisions or additions.

  8. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  9. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  10. CLOSED SESSION – None.

  11. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, March 3, 2026, at
  6:30 P.M. Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will be
  available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the City’s website at
  www.sangabrielcity.com.

MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 17, 2026
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Menchaca called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at
  6:31 P.M. on Tuesday, February 17, 2026, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South
  Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Council Member Wu.

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Tony Ding, Jorge Herrera Avila, John Wu, Vice Mayor
  Eric Chan, and Mayor Denise Menchaca.
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, Assistant City Attorney
  Martin Koczanowicz, Community Services Director

I
  Rebecca Perez, Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark, Fire Chief
  Steven Wallace, Finance Director William Kaholokula,
  Police Chief Edward Elizalde, Community Development
  Director David Sanchez, Public Works Director Michael
  Sledd, and Assistant City Clerk Adam Yang.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Mayor Menchaca wished everyone a Happy Lunar New Year.

  Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Mayor Menchaca approved the agenda order.

  2. PRESENTATIONS- None.

I  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Randye Kay, spoke in opposition to the construction of an Al data center in Monterey
  Park and requested a San Gabriel urgency ordinance for a moratorium on data centers.

  Grace Yang, San Gabriel Library Manager, invited all to pick up a red envelope and
  bookmark at the Library in celebration of the Year of the Horse and Lunar New Year;
  and to attend Paint Like Alma Thomas on February 21, 2026, from 3:00 -4:30 P.M. and
  Places in the Sun on February 25, 2026, from 3:00 - 4:00 P.M. in honor of African
  American and Black History Month.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 4  February 17, 2026
   Denise Gotch, resident, solicited the community for names of veterans who were born
  or lived in San Gabriel for inclusion on the future San Gabriel Veterans Memorial.

  Chasity Jennings-Nunez, resident, wished all a Happy Lunar New Year, reported on a
  reception for the Black History Month Art Exhibition at Blossom Market Hall, and
  expressed displeasure with the City Council for their silence on Immigration and
  Customs Enforcement (ICE) activities.

  Mandy Luu and Sherry Luu, residents, commented on a notice of code violation they

I  received, expressed dissatisfaction with their interaction with City code enforcement
  staff, and requested an extension to clean up their property.

  Athens Services Senior Vice President John Harrington introduced Athens' Vice
  President of Governmental Affairs Luis Ayala.

  Michael Cervantes, resident, requested that the Silent Film Festival series at the Mission
  Playhouse be expanded.

  Mary Garcia, resident, requested that Public Works address raised curbs at 1026 Euclid
  and 1036 S. Pine Street.

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  A motion was made by Council Member Wu, seconded by Council Member Ding, to
  approve Consent Calendar Items 4A - 4E as presented.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

I  AYES:
  NOES:
  ABSTAIN:
  DING, HERRERA AVILA, WU, CHAN, MENCHACA
  NONE
  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council approved:

  1. Minutes of the Special City Council Meeting of February 3, 2026.
  2. Minutes of the Regular City Council Meeting of February 3, 2026.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The City Council approved January 23 and 30, 2026, Material Demands for the
  payment of City expenditures.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT - JANUARY 2026

I  The City Council received and filed the Cash and Investment Report for January
  2026.

  D. EXCHANGE OF PROPOSITION A FUNDS IN THE AMOUNT OF $500,000

  The City Council approved and authorized the City Manager to execute the
  agreement with the Foothill Transit Authority authorizing the exchange of
  $500,000 in Proposition A Funds for $375,000 in General Fund revenue.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of4  February 17, 2026
   E. APPROVAL OF PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT AND STATEMENT OF
  WORK WITH CIVICPLUS FOR CITY WEBSITE REDESIGN, HOSTING, AND
  RELATED DIGITAL SERVICES

  The City Council authorized the City Manager to execute a Professional Services
  Agreement and associated Statement of Work with CivicPlus for the redesign,
  hosting, and ongoing support of the City of San Gabriel website, including related
  digital services.

I  5. PUBLIC HEARING - None.

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS - None.

  7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. REVIEW VETERANS MEMORIAL CONCEPTUAL DESIGNS AND PROVIDE
  DIRECTION TO STAFF AND LANDSCAPE ARCHITECT DAVID VOLZ DESIGN
  CREATIVE

  Community Services Director Perez made the staff presentation and Director of
  Design Gary Vasquez of David Volz Design Creative, presented the designs.

  Clarifying discussion included design elements, plant materials, lighting, security,
  anti-vandalism measures, manner and placement of veteran and sponsor names,
  and inclusion of Mission San Gabriel input.

  Theresa Olivas Justiniani, resident, founding member of the San Gabriel Veterans'
  Memorial Coalition, Michael A. Cervantes, President of the San Gabriel Veterans'

I  Memorial Coalition, and Denise Gotch, resident and Coalition member,
  commented on various aspects of the Memorial.

  Discussion included design preferences, qualifications for veteran name inclusion,
  landscape maintenance, and soliciting input from City Commissions.

  Mayor Menchaca reopened public comment.

  The following made additional comments regarding design elements, Coalition
  inclusion and communication, pedestrian safety, and a sign at the future site
  announcing the project: Mary Garcia, Debbie Cordero, Michael Cervantes, Patricia
  Foltyn, and Denise Gotch.

  There was a consensus of the City Council for Design 2 and staff was directed to
  solicit design input from the Design Review and Historic Preservation and Cultural
  Resource Commissions.

  8. CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

I  City Manager Lazzaretto wished all a Happy Lunar New Year.

  9. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Vice Mayor Chan reported on his attendance at the grand opening and ribbon cutting
  of Guiji Tea House at Tawa Gateway, IPAC officer's installation dinner, grand opening
  for Milk & Co Cafe in Monterey Park, Black History Month Art Exhibit at Blossom
  Market Hall, League of Women Voters 90th Anniversary Gala event at the Arcadia
  Community Center, Public Safety Summit hosted by Temple City Mayor Sternquist at

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of4  February 17, 2026
   the Temple City County Library; hoped everyone had a great President's Day; and
  wished all a Happy Lunar New Year.
  Council Member Herrera Avila wished all a Happy Chinese Lunar New Year.

  Council Member Ding reported on his attendance at the Guiji Tea grand opening,
  Auchel World/Grant Prospects Financial and Insurance Services event at the San
  Gabriel Sheraton, a cultural event hosted by a Pasadena church choir, attended the
  IPAC Officer's installation dinner, Guandong University event at San Gabriel Hilton, San
  Gabriel Valley Council of Governments (SGVCOG) 2028 Olympics Ad Hoc Committee

I  meeting, Jiangsu Chamber of Commerce Lunar New Year Celebration; and Hakka
  Cultural Celebration event.

  Council Member Wu reported on his attendance at a Lunar New Year Celebration at
  Hsi Lai Temple, Ramona Parlor dinner as a member of the Native Sons of the Golden
  West, a meeting of San Gabriel Valley Council of Governments (SGVCOG) 2028
  Olympics Ad Hoc Committee, and the inauguration of the American Chinese Cuisine
  Association at the Hilton San Gabriel; suggested moving San Gabriel's Dumpling and
  Beer Fest to July for the Olympics; and wished all a Happy New Year.

  Mayor Menchaca thanked staff for decorating the Council Chamber for Lunar New
  Year, wished all a Happy Lunar New Year, announced a Ramona Parlor, Native Sons of
  the Golden West fundraiser, reported she met with new management at the San
  Gabriel Hilton Hotel regarding the 2028 Olympics, and reported her attendance at a
  211 LA nonprofit lunch, National Association of Latino Elected and Appointed Officials
  (NALEO) 50th Anniversary event, and a League of Women Voters event.

  10. CLOSED SESSION - None.

I  11. ADJOURNMENT

  The meeting was adjourned at 9:01 P.M.

  Respectfully submitted:
